sourceObjects.text: Compute viscosity using the stress-tensor Kubo formula, the quadratic transverse-graviton effective action, conserved low-frequency radial momentum and infalling horizon conditions. Compute entropy density using Wald's Noether-charge formula, with horizon-binormal normalization εµν εµν=−2.

sourceRelations.statement: Restricted to the common nonextremal planar AdS5 Weyl-squared sector and first order in χ, the left appendix's calculation instantiates the radial-canonical-momentum horizon prescription and Wald entropy procedure described by the right endpoint. The displayed horizon kernels agree after κ_L²=8πG_R and sqrt(−g_rr/g_tt)=1/(r²ab), and the reported ratios agree as η/s=[1−8χ+4χq²/r0⁶]/(4π)+O(χ²). This is a method-instance relation, without a claim of historical borrowing. It excludes the nonzero left Weyl–Maxwell interaction, right curvature-cubed or second-order results, an independent derivation of the complete Kubo-to-momentum chain, equivalence of unprinted binormal definitions, and transfer of WGC or KSS constraints.

intersection.statement: A common action exists in the Weyl-squared sector: set left c2=0, write left c1=χ, and set right b2=χ, b1=−5χ/6, b3=8χ/3, c1=c2=0. Compare only terms linear in χ.

Both calculations concern an isotropic planar five-dimensional charged AdS background and its transverse shear fluctuation. Restrict this comparison to the zero-spatial-momentum, low-frequency prescription at a regular nonextremal horizon.

required_assumptions.statement: Impose the stated common-action coupling restrictions and retain only first order in the perturbative parameter χ.
Use r0>0 and x=q²/r0⁶<2, with 2−x held positive as χ tends to zero, so the comparison does not require an interchange of the extremal and low-frequency limits.

Compare the separately reported canonical-momentum horizon formulas in the same displayed quadratic-action basis. The right source supplies the conservation and infalling implementation; an independent derivation of these conditions for the left calculation is not asserted.

satisfied_assumptions.statement: The common-action restrictions are explicit algebraic choices within the displayed actions. They produce the same Weyl-squared invariant without a field redefinition and contain no derivatives of curvature.
The supplied metric ansätze and zeroth-order temperature formulas support the selected planar nonextremal background sector.
The displayed quadratic actions have the same six monomial structures, and the two reported horizon formulas have matching kernels after the metric and gravitational-normalization substitutions.

scope_mismatches.statement: The left appendix also permits a Weyl–Maxwell interaction, whereas the right toy model excludes higher-derivative Maxwell terms. This interaction is set to zero in the asserted overlap.

The left appendix gives a leading-order calculation using the zeroth-order background. The right calculation retains curvature-cubed and quadratic four-derivative-coupling contributions and uses corrected metric data. Those higher-order applications are excluded.
The left main-text Riemann-squared action and its appendix Weyl-squared action are distinct. The asserted overlap uses the appendix action.

conventions.conversion: Compare the displayed five-dimensional bulk theories in unit AdS-radius conventions and each source's unit-boundary-speed frame. No conversion of dimensionful transport coefficients between unnormalized time coordinates is asserted.
conventions.left_definition: The left sets the AdS radius and boundary speed to one.
conventions.right_definition: The right sets the uncorrected AdS radius to one and describes the time rescaling needed for unit boundary speed.

conventions.conversion: Identify κ_L²=8πG_R and choose −2Λ_R=12 in the common action. The gravitational constant κ_L² is distinct from the horizon kernels denoted κ2 and κ4.
conventions.left_definition: The bulk action carries 1/(2κ_L²), with Einstein term R+12.
conventions.right_definition: The bulk action carries 1/(16πG_R), with Einstein term R−2Λ_R.

conventions.concept: Common curvature invariant and coupling names
conventions.conversion: Set χ=c1_L, c2_L=0; b2_R=χ, b1_R=−5χ/6, b3_R=8χ/3, c1_R=c2_R=0. Then the right quadratic curvature correction is χ[Riemann²−(4/3)Ricci²+R²/6]=χ Weyl². Identically named c_i across papers are not identified.
conventions.left_definition: Appendix c1_L multiplies Weyl²; c2_L multiplies a Weyl–Maxwell interaction.
conventions.right_definition: The b_i multiply curvature-squared invariants, while c1_R and c2_R multiply curvature-cubed invariants.

conventions.concept: Radial metric and positive exterior root
conventions.conversion: With left c_metric(r)=r, set Ω_R=r²a² and σ_R=a/b. Then U≡sqrt(−g_rr/g_tt)=σ_R/Ω_R=1/(r²ab), taking the positive exterior root. Here Ω_R renames the right metric function ω(r), avoiding confusion with frequency.

conventions.concept: Shear mode, Fourier convention and quadratic coefficients
conventions.conversion: Identify the mixed-index shear field φ and use [dk]=d⁴k/(2π)⁴. A through F denote coefficients of the same displayed monomials, not higher-derivative couplings. Primes denote d/dr.
conventions.left_definition: h^y_x is expanded as φ_k(r)exp(−iωt+ikz); the quadratic action contains Aφ''φ, Bφ'φ', Cφ'φ, Dφφ, Eφ''φ'', Fφ''φ' and a boundary term.
conventions.right_definition: The same mixed-index field and Fourier sign appear, with the same quadratic monomial basis and boundary terms.

conventions.conversion: Both separately report η=lim Π/(iωφ). With K2=U(A−B+F'/2) and K4=(EU')', the left η=(K2+K4)/κ_L² and right η=(K2+K4)/(8πG_R) coincide under the dictionary. Image:2 resolves the left derivatives and prefactor in equations (32)–(33).
conventions.left_definition: Equations (29), (32) and (33) give the boundary momentum ratio and its horizon expression.
conventions.right_definition: Equations (3.9)–(3.13) report low-frequency momentum conservation, infalling conditions and the horizon expression.

conventions.conversion: Compare the named Wald prescription and reported entropy densities. Their Einstein terms agree: 2πr0³/κ_L²=r0³/(4G_R). The right's explicit binormal normalization is recorded; an independently verified left binormal definition is not asserted.
conventions.left_definition: The appendix invokes Wald's formula and reports the density in (35) and (39), without an explicit binormal normalization in the supplied appendix text.
conventions.right_definition: Equations (3.16)–(3.18) use −2π times the horizon integral of ∂L/∂R contracted with two binormals, with ε_μν ε^μν=−2; entropy is divided by planar spatial volume. Image:5 confirms the sign and normalization.

conventions.concept: Charge parameters, horizon scheme and perturbative order
conventions.conversion: For the ratio check identify q_L²=q_R² and x=q²/r0⁶. The right's bar-x=bar-q² equals x+O(χ), so replacing bar-x by x in an already O(χ) correction changes only O(χ²). No signed gauge-potential identification is needed.
conventions.left_definition: The appendix uses q²/r0⁶ and retains first order in its higher-derivative couplings.
conventions.right_definition: Tilde-q=q/r0³ uses the fixed horizon radius; bar-q=q/bar-r0³ uses the parameter introduced to compare at fixed physical temperature.
